chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "It is disliked to combine two Surahs in the obligatory prayer, but as for the voluntary prayer, there is no objection."

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: there is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine two Surahs in one Rak'ah of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chain of Zurarah clarifies the juristic distinction between obligatory and voluntary prayers regarding the recitation of two Surahs; while combining them into a single continuous recitation is disliked (makruh) in Fard prayers to maintain the distinctness of each unit, it is fully permissible in Nafl prayers. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the structural integrity of the Fard prayer while allowing flexibility in voluntary acts of worship.
